title: EXP-122 - Hello World Part 8 Phase 4b: GridOrders' Four Property-Bound Columns and Read-Only/Disable, plus the StaticCart Width Correction, on FX_CustomerPortal, with a Close/Reopen Readback
objective: Finish Hello World Part 8 Phase 4 (08:26-09:47) on FX_CustomerPortal (User scope), FlexLayoutMain > Region04: cartpage: correct StaticCart's Width to 20 (EXP-121 finding 1: it reads 29.559322033898304 after reopen); give GridOrders four GridColumns through its Edit grid column(s) dialog (the two Designer-created gridColumn3_USER and gridColumn4_USER plus two added with the dialog's New control), named GridColOrdNum, GridColItem, GridColCount and GridColCustID in dialog order, each with Binding Type Property bound to object.FX_OrderNumber, object.FX_Item, object.FX_Count and object.FX_CustomerID; set GridOrders' Behavior Read-Only/Disable to True. The narrated Regenerate is not needed (EXP-118). T1 gate; T2 StaticCart Width; T3 add and rename the columns; T4 bind the first two; T5 bind the last two; T6 Read-Only/Disable; T7 close/reopen readback and final audit. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md (the repository file, at the start of every task), docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt8.md Phase 4 (lines 135-153) and transcript lines 396-409 (08:19-09:47), recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-121, EXP-120 and EXP-068-R2 records. Read nothing else: no other records and no later Part 8 phases. In a continuation task, AGENTS.md and the current task's part of this record are enough.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-122-hello-world-part-8-phase-4b-grid-orders-columns.md and evidence/EXP-122/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If a session expiry, logout card or sign-in page appears, record it and stop for the operator (EXP-107: the operator signs in manually); do not navigate, type credentials or screenshot a filled sign-in form. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, dialog, menu or unsaved change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action. Signed-out session (EXP-116): a server-event error together with a portal tab reading 'Logout Successful' means the session ended; record it and stop for the operator.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget (EXP-109, EXP-111): if a task cannot finish, stop only at a step boundary right after a Save (never with an unsaved change, open list, editor or dialog) and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T7; if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log. A Caption commit that leaves Save disabled is also a stop signal (EXP-110-R2): record it and stop blocked before any further click.

Editing scope: stay in User scope throughout. If an 'Identify Your Editing Scope' dialog appears, confirm it shows User for the signed-in user and accept it unchanged; if it shows any other scope, Cancel it and stop blocked.

Designer gate (T1, read-only except at most one Form open): User scope; FX_CustomerPortal open and clean (Save disabled), no dialog open; if another Form tab is active, select FX_CustomerPortal's tab; if it is not open, open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (never Select Form OK). Record the Components tree under FlexLayoutMain > Region04: cartpage, expected in order: StaticCart, GridOrders (Data Source objects) with exactly two child GridColumns gridColumn3_USER and gridColumn4_USER, ButtonCheckout; if it differs, record it and stop blocked. Select (Components row Type cell) and read, without editing: StaticCart's Layout (expected Size 29.5593220338983; 1.5, Width 29.559322033898304, Height 1.5); GridOrders' Binding Type and Binding (expected Primary Collection Grid, objects) and its Behavior Read-Only/Disable value; each of gridColumn3_USER and gridColumn4_USER: Caption, Binding Type and Binding. Expanding property groups is view only. Record the baseline console error count and one screenshot of the tree with GridOrders' Properties.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task. Snapshot size (EXP-114): if an untargeted snapshot is too large to return inline, take targeted snapshots of the needed panel instead (record that); never save snapshots to files.

Property rules (EXP-111, EXP-120, EXP-121): select a component by its Components row (click its Type cell; a Name-cell click after reopen may not select) and confirm the Properties header names it (labels lag: also confirm the Name row). Lists (Binding Type, Binding, Read-Only/Disable): open the list with its arrow and click the planned option, then leave the field by clicking the Description row (never Tab or arrow keys while a list is open); if the arrow is not exposed, a value-cell double-click may show it; if the planned option is absent, close the list without choosing and stop blocked before the Save. Text fields (Name, Width): click the value cell, one plain fill, one Tab; verify the field reads the planned value. At most one correction per field. Record the console error count after each action. After each performed step exactly one Designer Save, recording its response and the Save state. Answer an OK-only informational prompt (for example 'You will need to regen this form ...' or 'No object name given.') with OK and record it verbatim; any other prompt not covered here: record it, choose the non-changing answer (No or Cancel) and stop blocked. Leave every other property unchanged (column Captions, Sizes, Locations and Tab order stay at their defaults).

StaticCart Width (T2): select StaticCart, expand Layout and Size (view only). Width must read 29.559322033898304 (a real change, EXP-121 finding 1; if it already reads 20, record it, make no entry and no Save). Fill Width 20 once and Tab; record Width and the Size summary (expected 20; 1.5) and Height (1.5, not edited). If Width does not read 20, use the one correction; if it still does not, stop blocked before the Save. If Width reads 20 but the summary differs, record both exactly and Save anyway (T7 decides persistence). One Designer Save. Screenshots: Layout before the entry; Layout before the Save; the Save response state.

GridOrders columns (T3; EXP-068-R2 route): select GridOrders by its Components row; on the canvas a blue icon appears at the top left of the grid (tooltip 'Edit grid column(s)'); click it once (coordinate click; hover first to confirm the tooltip). The dialog 'Contained Components' must list exactly gridColumn3_USER and gridColumn4_USER; if it lists other rows or another title, Cancel and stop blocked. Select the last row (gridColumn4_USER) and click the dialog's New control (+, tooltip 'New') once: exactly one row is added; record its name and position; with the last row selected click New once more; the dialog must then list exactly four rows (record their order). Then, in dialog row order, select each row and rename it through the dialog's Name value cell (plain fill, Tab, verify the row label): row 1 GridColOrdNum, row 2 GridColItem, row 3 GridColCount, row 4 GridColCustID. Do not touch any other property in the dialog (no Binding Type, Binding or Caption). OK once (the dialog closes with no message, EXP-068-R2). Verify the Components tree under GridOrders lists the four names in that order and that Save is enabled; one Designer Save. Screenshots: the dialog at open; the dialog with four rows before renaming; the dialog with the four names before OK; the tree before the Save; the Save response state.

Column bindings (T4: GridColOrdNum, GridColItem; T5: GridColCount, GridColCustID; one column per step, EXP-068-R2 route): select the column by its Components row (Type cell); expand Data Source (view only); Binding Type list: click Property, Description-row commit; the Binding may then show an auto-assigned value such as object._ItemId (EXP-068-R2; record it and do not keep it); open the Binding list with its arrow and click exactly the planned option (GridColOrdNum object.FX_OrderNumber; GridColItem object.FX_Item; GridColCount object.FX_Count; GridColCustID object.FX_CustomerID; never a longer name that starts with it, never the variables.FX_Count variable), Description-row commit; verify Binding Type Property and the exact Binding; one Designer Save per column. The Components-list Data Source cell may lag until reopen (EXP-068-R2): record it, do not try to force it. Screenshots per column: the Binding list open; Binding Type and Binding before the Save; the Save response state.

GridOrders Read-Only/Disable (T6): select GridOrders by its Components row; expand Behavior (view only); record its rows; open the Read-Only/Disable list and click True, Description-row commit; verify it reads True; one Designer Save. If no Behavior row named Read-Only/Disable exists, record the Behavior rows and stop blocked before any change. Screenshots: Behavior before the change; the value before the Save; the Save response state.

Readback and audit (T7, one task): close the clean FX_CustomerPortal once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text), reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry, record the Components tree under Region04: cartpage (StaticCart; GridOrders with GridColOrdNum, GridColItem, GridColCount, GridColCustID in that order with their Data Source cells; ButtonCheckout; nothing else changed), then select and read: StaticCart's Width and Size summary; GridOrders' Binding Type, Binding and Read-Only/Disable; each column's Name, Binding Type and Binding. Record what the canvas shows for GridOrders in the cartpage column. Open no dialog or list. Leave FX_CustomerPortal open and clean. Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory and the final state. Screenshots: the reopened tree with the cartpage rows; StaticCart's Layout; GridOrders' Behavior and Data Source; one per column's Data Source.

Before every click, use references from the most recent snapshot taken in the current task (not from find output); after any timeout or 'Ref not found', take one fresh untargeted snapshot and use only its references (one per error). ExtJS comboboxes are not <select> elements (EXP-101): open their list and click the option. Coordinates are allowed only for the one 'Edit grid column(s)' icon click on the canvas grid (T3) and, once per field, for a list arrow that has no reference; record each such click. Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; never leave a prompt, list, editor or dialog open across tasks. Classify findings as observed only.
